obernants.operator: brute enumerates all vertex subsets and tests every unordered pair against the supplied edge list; it does not use production neighbors, pivot selection, maximal-clique traversal or pruning. It ranks feasible subsets by cardinality then vector lexicographic order. All 1100 simple graphs through n=5 include a triangle with an isolated vertex, distinguishing maximal from maximum, and graphs with tied largest cliques, distinguishing size-only selection from the specified canonical set.

obernants.operator: lexicographic_maximum_and_bit_63 asserts [0,2] for edges [(0,2),(1,2),(1,3)], so a later tied clique [1,2] or [1,3] is rejected; the compiled candidate>best mutant fails this named test. On the same fixed universe, complementing edges turns those size-two cliques into independent sets without changing lexicographic ranking. This specialization constrains the clique/independent-set identity mathematically; the owned tests execute clique enumeration, while the complement join belongs to the integration harness. No independent-set native coverage is inferred here.
